tn_g_the_dispensary.blurb: The Dispensary is one of the walls at Woodcock Cove, a sandstone cliff band outside Dunlap on the western edge of the Sequatchie Valley. The focus is a free-standing tower, found by taking the trail from the lot and then dropping down the ladders. Of the eleven routes, ten are bolted and one is trad, and nothing here is easy: about five sit in the 5.11s, four in the 5.12s, and two reach 5.13. Most lines look north, so they catch a bit of morning and evening light and sit in shade in between, which helps on warm days. Star ratings on the lines are mostly high.

tn_f_capitol_wall.blurb: Capitol Wall is a tall sandstone face at Woodcock Cove near Dunlap, a short stroll beyond the Dispensary once you are down the ladders and heading to the right. It holds ten bolted routes, so it is a sport wall for people who are already comfortable on steeper, harder ground: one climb in the 5.10s, three in the 5.11s, five in the 5.12s and one 5.13. The lower part of the wall is loose and poor, so expect the good climbing to start higher up.

tn_a_the_zoo.blurb: The Zoo is a south-facing sandstone wall at the far west end of the developed climbing at Woodcock Cove, near Dunlap. It is the longest walk of the Woodcock walls: past the ladders, then right, and around a corner after a small stream crossing. Ten sport routes run from one easy line in the 5.7 range through a couple of 5.9s and a 5.10 to a solid block of 5.11s and 5.12s, so there is something for intermediate leaders as well as people pushing harder. Being south-facing, it takes sun and makes more sense on cool days.

tn_main_cave.blurb: Main Cave is the headline section of Sucka Cave, a small crag on Suck Creek Road as it drops toward the Sequatchie Valley outside Chattanooga. It holds the longest, steepest and hardest climbs at the cliff, all of them sport and mostly roofs and overhangs. Of eleven routes, three are 5.11, one is 5.12 and seven are 5.13, so this is a wall for strong climbers rather than beginners. A short uphill trail from the main pull-off leads straight to the cave. Routes here are only about 30 to 40 feet tall, which suits a quick evening session.

tn_image_wall.blurb: Image Wall is the first wall you meet after the steep descent into South Clear Creek, in the Obed and Clear Creek climbing area of eastern Tennessee. Ten of its eleven routes are sport, with one trad line, and the range is friendly to a mixed group: a couple of easy routes in the 5.7 and 5.8 range, two 5.9s, two 5.10s, four 5.11s and one 5.12. South Clear Creek in general is a busy destination and gets hot in summer, so cooler months are the better bet. Expect a trail walk of roughly a quarter hour from the lot before the drop.

_expect.name: Bonny and Clyde Wall- AKA Drifters Wall

tn_bonny_and_clyde_wall_aka_drifters_wal.blurb: Bonny and Clyde Wall, also called Drifters Wall, sits on Castle Rock, the orange sandstone bluff above Jasper that works well as a winter crag. It is a vertical, heavily featured face, quieter than the neighboring Predator Wall, and reached with a minute or so of walking past that wall. Ten of the eleven routes are sport and one is trad. The wall gets harder as you go up: three 5.9s, two 5.11s, four 5.12s and two 5.13s, so a few warm-up lines lead into some serious sport projects for strong climbers.
